claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 accurately sets out the statutory definition of 'individualized education program' (IEP) in 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(A), faithfully incorporating all statutory components (I) through (VIII) including present levels, measurable annual goals, progress reporting, special education and related services, extent of nonparticipation with nondisabled peers, testing accommodations/alternate assessments, service commencement details, and transition requirements.

Claim C0001 captures the rule of construction in 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(A)(ii)(I) providing that nothing in the section shall be construed to require additional information beyond what is explicitly required in the section.

Claim C0002 accurately articulates the rule of construction in 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(A)(ii)(II) that the IEP Team is not required to include information under one component of an IEP that is already contained under another component.

Claim C0003 correctly defines 'individualized education program team' or 'IEP Team' pursuant to 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(B), detailing each required and permissive member across clauses (i) through (vii).

Claim C0004 faithfully reflects 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(C)(i), exempting an IEP Team member from meeting attendance when the parent and agency agree the attendance is not necessary because the member's area is not modified or discussed.

Claim C0005 accurately represents 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(C)(ii), covering permissive excusal of an IEP Team member when their area is modified or discussed, subject to written input and parent/agency consent.
Claim C0006 accurately states the statutory requirement under 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(C)(iii) that a parent's agreement under clause (i) and consent under clause (ii) must be in writing.
Claim C0007 correctly sets forth 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(D), requiring an invitation to the initial IEP meeting to be sent to the subchapter III service coordinator/representative upon parental request.
